name: GTPL Hathway Ltd
title: GTPL Hathway Ltd - 540602 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Cable/broadband operator posted a Q4 loss on one-offs, subscriber growth stalled, and management guides capex to ~INR350 crore a year with no near-term reduction, so supply is expanding into a flat base.

summary.headline: GTPL Hathway swung to a Q4 FY26 net loss as consolidated reported EBITDA margin fell to 9.7% and operating margin to 18%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 4% YoY to INR9,344 million, but the quarter posted negative PAT driven by two fewer operating days (~INR12 crore revenue impact), year-end impairment/provisions (~INR7.5-8 crore) and a forex revaluation loss (~INR9 crore). FY26 consolidated revenue grew 7% to INR37,466 million, with net profit attributable to parent of INR156 million. Subscriber base was flat in the quarter as capex shifted to the Headend-In-The-Sky (HITS) platform, and management guided to renewed consolidation and capex of about INR350 crore per year.

financial_highlights.change: FY26 operating margin 22%, prior year cited as 24-25% in 2022-23

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated net profit attributable to parent (FY26)

financial_highlights.change: company stated free cash flow positive

financial_highlights.value: 20% of face value INR2 per share

segments.name: Cable TV
segments.commentary: Digital cable subscribers 9.40 million, of which 8.70 million paying, with no net growth in the quarter; management attributes this to HITS migration focus and reduced acquisitions. Churn stated at 17-18% versus industry 20-21%.

segments.name: Broadband
segments.commentary: Active subscribers 1.06 million, adding 15,000 YoY for the year; Q4 net adds described as muted. Q4 ARPU INR465 (about INR440 three years ago); homepass 5.95 million, 75% FTTX-ready; data usage 436 GB/month, +10% YoY.

guidance_outlook: Next year (FY27) capex guided at about INR350 crore, with about INR150-160 crore for broadband and the rest for cable and HITS; FY27-FY29 capex about INR700 crore over two years, split 50% maintenance and 50% growth.
Management does not expect capex to decline for at least three years, citing growth opportunities in cable, HITS and broadband.
Management expects renewed net additions in cable and broadband from Q1 FY27 as HITS scales, and expects cost savings in delivery costs to lift EBITDA.
Targets ROCE recovery to about 15% within 2-3 years; expects PAT to return toward the earlier peak of about INR200 crore in 3-4 years.
Plans annual ARPU increases of INR3-5 (about 3-4%), with cumulative 10-12% over three years; prioritises volume over value.
Says management expects more consolidation announcements, with named deals possibly disclosed by the next quarterly call; no quantified target given.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR290 crore: about INR110 crore broadband and about INR180 crore cable and HITS.
HITS platform launched as GTPL Infinity; uplinking centre and downlinking capex underway; company says a new market can be launched in 7-10 days.
Broadband homepass 5.95 million; conversion of homepass to paying customers at about 17-18% against an industry norm of about 20%.
Transponder contracts for HITS are USD-denominated, creating forex revaluation exposure; accounted under depreciation and ROU assets.
demand_pricing: Cable subscriber base flat in Q4; company says it is retaining base amid high competition and an unfavourable environment for cable.
Broadband competition from AirFiber (fixed wireless) hit net adds; management says net adds have started recovering.
Broadband ARPU rose to INR465 on higher-speed package migration, though package prices were cut slightly; about INR25 uplift reported in the last two days before the call.

Management sees 40-45 million subscribers with small MSOs as acquisition targets and about 40-50 million Free Dish households as addressable via HITS; about 130-140 million households remain without TV.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no subscriber growth in cable and broadband this quarter, and are the exceptional items recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Cable focus shifted to converting the base and HITS cost savings, with expansion from Q1 FY27; broadband net adds were muted but are expected to resume next quarter. The impairment was described as a one-time item on old analogue-era investments.

qa_highlights.question: How long can industry consolidation last, and what has held back other HITS adopters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 40-45 million subscribers sit with small MSOs and that consolidation will accelerate post-HITS launch, with about 800 MSOs in India. Competition is defined broadly to include OTT, telcos and social platforms.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 40-45 million small-MSO base can be acquired in FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, saying talks are underway with large players and that deal announcements should come by next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the quarter's operating margin drop from 22% to 18% due to one-offs above the line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 18% is affected by the two-day shortfall (Q4 has 90 days versus 92 in Q3, when margin was 24%); the one-time items sit below EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27-FY29 and the maintenance versus growth split?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR350 crore per year, with about INR150 crore for broadband and about INR200 crore for cable and HITS; about 50% maintenance and 50% growth, totalling about INR700 crore over two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says normalised ROCE is about 15%, and expects to return to that level in 2-3 years as growth capex is deployed; FY26 ROCE was in single digits.

risks_watch: Negative Q4 PAT: management said the INR9 crore forex loss relates to USD-denominated HITS transponder contracts, with exposure to INR movements.
Operating margin trend: down from 24-25% (2022-23) to 22% (FY26) and 18% in Q4 FY26; the company says HITS savings should reverse this.
Acquisition pipeline has no quantified targets or disclosed deals; the next quarterly call is expected to reveal first announcements.
Broadband net adds were muted in Q4 and competition from AirFiber remains a factor.
Capex stepping up to about INR350 crore per year with no reduction for at least three years; ROCE in single digits in FY26 against a 15% target.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term HITS and consolidation strategy, but defensive on the quarter's loss and margin decline, which management attributed to one-offs and the shorter quarter. Evasive on acquisition scale and timing, declining to quantify subscriber targets.
key_quotes: This quarter has become exceptional as the company has reported negative profit after tax.
We are more going or playing the volume game rather than the value game here.
So that's why we have not gone for the very aggressive consolidation and all, which we used to do it from last two to three years.
So I'm not looking forward for at least for next 3 years that we will going to reduce our capex.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term HITS, consolidation and ARPU strategy and on the INR350 crore capex plan, but defensive on the Q4 net loss, margin fall and flat subscribers; analysts pushed on the one-off items, the acquisition scale and timing, and the margin and ROCE recovery path.
